title: The River in the Memory Ice

goal.text: Compare your crossing with the yetis' memory ice.

steps.label: Show a newcomer how to look

plate.narration: Deep in the glacier, yeti hands have carved a room from blue ice. Lantern light slides along the walls. Some of the ice shines with pictures too faint to read.

arrival.narration: An elder yeti welcomes you into a room cut from the glacier. The route worker from the valley has come too. Behind a low table, water moves inside a pale wall of ice. It is a remembered river. "Help us compare that view with the river you crossed," says the elder. "We have looked at it three times and filed it three different ways." Pip keeps his tail well away from the tea.

variants.text: Pip lays down your account. It says you crossed by the high rock reach.
Pip lays down your account of the supported low-shelf crossing.

quiet_rule.narration: The elder sets down the tea. "Do not shout near the old ice; you do not know what you might wake." You agree to raise a hand when you need a pause. Pip whispers so quietly that nobody can hear him at all.

witness_first.narration: The route worker gives the elder a drawing of the two valleys. Pip lays your crossing sketch beside it. Where should the telling start?

witness_first_1.narration: The worker tells what she saw from her bank. You tell only the crossing you made. Pip points out where the two stories overlap. The elder keeps them as two stories, not one.

witness_first_2.narration: You point out the chipped marker and two ridges on both pages. The worker agrees before anyone talks about the water. Pip marks the parts the spray hid.

catalog_cards.narration: The elder joins a standing-place card, a ridge sketch and a water account. A younger keeper peeks over her shoulder. Pip lines the cards up like birthdays. "Three visits," the elder corrects him. "The river did not leave us a birthday." The cards say where to look, not how old the river is.

listening_floor.narration: A faint low song travels through the floor from a hall elsewhere in the ice. Pip feels it in his paws. "My toes are humming." The elder shows you two marked places where readers can watch the memory.

support_ice.narration: The close reading place needs a settled cradle to catch flakes. Prop it up and the view will be clearer, but meltwater drips near the papers. Or set up the dry table farther back. The view is cloudier, but the papers stay safe. Which will you ready?

support_ice_1.narration: You ask the elder where the wooden cradle can take a push. Then you slide a wedge under it from the marked floor. Nobody touches the memory ice.

support_ice_1_check.narration: A support shifts beside the ice. Hold it while the tie goes on. A tiny crack ticks above you. Everyone stops chatting.

interaction.cue: Hold the support while the tie is secured.

support_ice_1_done.narration: The cradle stays steady when the elder gives it a gentle test. Now you can look without balancing on anything wobbly.

support_ice_1_changed.narration: The corner shifts! Everyone steps back while the elder props it with a board. You move the standing place farther away and mark the wobbly corner off limits.

support_ice_2.narration: You move only the loose standing mat, far from the ice. The elder checks that you can still see the memory from there.

support_ice_2_check.narration: Level the wide dry table at the far viewpoint. The keeper puts the blank slips well away from the meltwater.

support_ice_2_done.narration: The far table is level and dry. The papers are safe. The view is cloudy, so you will need to look carefully.

support_ice_2_changed.narration: The elder steadies the far table with a spare wedge. It is dry and ready. The view is still cloudy.

first_memory.narration: The pale ice clears. A remembered river flows between familiar ridges, into the valley your sketch showed dry. Will you split up the watching, or all follow one landmark?

first_memory_1.narration: Pip watches the ridges while your party follows the water. Pip writes down every word, and where everyone stood. Nobody changes an account just to make it match.

first_memory_2.narration: Everyone picks the fork-shaped ridge and watches where the water leaves beside it. Nobody fills in the blanks with a made-up map.

second_view.narration: The elder leads you to a second marked viewpoint, still on the safe floor. A shiny reflection slides across the river. "Look again," says the elder. "Does it still look the same?"

second_view_1.narration: You hold Pip's sketch upright. You match its shapes to the ice, one bend at a time. Nobody turns the drawing just to make the river agree.

second_view_1_check.narration: A reflection slides across the remembered ridge. Keep your eye on the marked ridge as the cloudy layers swap places.

interaction.cue: Follow the marked ridge view through the moving cloudy layers.

second_view_1_done.narration: The two ridge profiles agree from both safe viewpoints. The reflection slides away, but the ridges stay put. Your own eyes found the match. Pip marks where you stood.

second_view_1_changed.narration: The reflection hides the middle bend, so you leave it blank. From the elder's side view, you can see the river leave by the other valley. She offers to sign that part if you want to use it.

second_view_2.narration: You pick three rocks that stay in view. Pip writes down their order only after the water has passed.

second_view_2_check.narration: The river passes three rocks in the moving view. Watch their order, then show it.

interaction.cue: Watch the rock passage, then echo it.

second_view_2_done.narration: You see the water pass the three rocks in order. The second viewpoint shows the same, even with a reflection sliding the other way. Pip numbers the rocks, not the years.

second_view_2_changed.narration: The reflection hides the middle bend, so you leave it blank. From the elder's side view, you can see the river leave by the other valley. She offers to sign that part if you want to use it.

what_matches.narration: The outside drawing and memory account lie on the elder's table. Pip points from one to the other. "Both show the river in that other valley!" What will your account say?

variants.text: You checked the river's direction yourselves.
The middle bend is still blank.

what_matches_1.narration: You write down the river's direction and leave its age and cause blank. The elder asks you to point to your proof before Pip copies it down.

variants.text: Your proof is the three rocks, in order.
Your proof is the two ridges and where you stood.

what_matches_2.narration: You write that the ice shows one old river, and you only saw a short change outside. The shared landmarks still make the match useful. The elder adds the river's direction underneath.

catalog_test.narration: A younger yeti keeper brings a fresh catalog slip. "I need a route from a visitor's question to the checked view," she explains. Can she find it on her own? Where should her search start?

variants.text: She has to find both places where you stood.
She has to find your proof with no hints.
The elder's signature tells her who to ask, but not a date.

catalog_test_1.narration: You hand the keeper your outside sketch. Can she find the matching memory? Pip zips his mouth shut so he cannot help.

catalog_test_1_check.narration: The younger keeper follows your cards from a visitor's question. Link the clues so she reaches the right view. The date she looked is not the river's age.

interaction.cue: Link the visitor question to the evidence.
clues: Start with what the visitor asks.
The catalog cross-reference connects the question to a viewpoint.
Finish at the checked viewpoint, not at a guessed date.

catalog_test_1_done.narration: The younger keeper follows the cards to both accounts without a keeper guiding her. She does not mix up the crossing and the old memory. "I could post a visitor guide," she offers.

catalog_test_1_changed.narration: The younger keeper mixes up the day she looked with the river's age. You fix the label together, but she still needs the elder's help. "I will sit with the next reader," she says. Visitors will need a keeper beside them.

catalog_test_2.narration: You hand the keeper the memory notes. Can they lead her to the worker's own story of today? The worker waits to see.

catalog_test_2_check.narration: The younger keeper follows your cards from a visitor's question. Link the clues so she reaches the right view. The date she looked is not the river's age.

interaction.cue: Link the visitor question to the evidence.
clues: Start with what the visitor asks.
The catalog cross-reference connects the question to a viewpoint.
Finish at the checked viewpoint, not at a guessed date.

catalog_test_2_done.narration: The younger keeper follows the cards to both accounts without a keeper guiding her. She does not mix up the crossing and the old memory. "I could post a visitor guide," she offers.

catalog_test_2_changed.narration: The younger keeper mixes up the day she looked with the river's age. You fix the label together, but she still needs the elder's help. "I will sit with the next reader," she says. Visitors will need a keeper beside them.

sliding_tray.narration: A shallow tray holds blank slips and chalk. Near the close view, meltwater has it sliding toward the table edge. "It's escaping!" squeaks Pip. If you set up the dry table, the slips are already safe over there. What will you do?

sliding_tray_1.narration: Pip shoves a stool out of the way. You keep your feet on the marked floor and reach for the tray. The elder stands between you and the old ice.

sliding_tray_1_check.narration: The tray tilts. Slips creep toward its edge. Level it together before the notes become a very small avalanche.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side until the load is level.

sliding_tray_1_done.narration: The slips and chalk go back on the table. Nobody left the safe floor. Pip laughs at how carefully everyone saved the blank paper.

sliding_tray_1_changed.narration: The tray bumps the table before you catch it. Two blank slips get wet, and the younger keeper hangs them up to dry. The written accounts are safe.

compare_accounts.narration: The elder asks whether your party has another checked observation of a river where today's geography does not fit it. Nobody has to invent one. This memory is already a clue: a river once left by a different valley. What will you do with clues from other places?

variants.text: At the Saltrot's buried bridge, your party found a waterline and rounded river pebbles under dry arches. That is another checked clue. It does not prove both changes happened together.

compare_accounts_1.narration: You name only what someone else could check. Clues from other places stay with their own names. The elder leaves a blank where nothing has been compared.

compare_accounts_2.narration: You keep this river on its own page. Pip marks a space where another clue could go later. The elder agrees. No guessing today.

claim_limit.narration: Pip reads the draft. The matched river is there. Its age and cause are still blank. "A blank is easier to fix than a confident mistake," says the elder. What question should you leave beside the clue?

record_choice.narration: The elder offers to keep a copy of your party's finished comparison. You can share it or keep it private. How the keeper's search went decides what kind of copy it can be.

variants.text: The keeper found her way alone, so it can be posted as a guide.
The keeper needed help, so visitors will need a keeper too.

record_choice_1.narration: You check the elder's copy against your page. Both show the river and the open questions. The younger keeper files it only after every hero has had a chance to fix it.

record_choice_2.narration: You thank the elder and keep your page. She agrees the words are yours to share. The younger keeper files only the room's own notes.

teach_back.narration: An arriving yeti visitor waits at the warm cup. "Where is a safe way to look?" the newcomer asks. You can show the room's own landmarks, or use a copy you chose to share.

variants.text: The newcomer grabs your posted guide while the keeper watches.
The keeper has your copy ready and will go along.
Your private page stays in your pack.
Your proof has to be part of the lesson.

rest.narration: Your river crossing and the memory agree on another valley. The date and cause are still unknown. Pip checks twice. "The drawing goes in the traveling pages, not my tea-stained scrap." You can rest, go back to the workers by the upper path, or head deeper into the glacier.

variants.text: Your posted guide stays up. The younger keeper helps any visitor who gets stuck.
The keeper keeps your shared copy for visitors who have help.
No copy of your private account is filed. The elder keeps her own notes.
The visitor found the view with no keeper's help.
The close cradle stays ready for the next reader.
The dry table keeps the next slips safe from meltwater.

second_view_prepared.narration: Your two watchers open their notes. One followed the water. The other kept the ridges fixed. The elder asks each watcher where they stood.

second_view_prepared_check.narration: Put the ridge notes and water notes together to rebuild the river's path. Pip covers his own page so it cannot copy yours.

clues: The ridge observer saw the fork before the bend.
The water observer saw the bend before the flat rock.
Both accounts place the flat rock last.

what_matches_keeper.narration: You ask the elder to read the river's direction with you and sign it. She watches from her side view, then signs just that part. Your own notes stay marked as yours.

variants.text: Your middle bend stays blank. The elder's side view fills it in.
You checked it yourselves, too. Her signature sits beside your own proof.

catalog_endorsed.narration: You give the younger keeper the elder's signed card. Can she follow it to the right view? The signature says who helped read it. It does not give a date.

catalog_endorsed_check.narration: The signed card leads the younger keeper to her seat and the checked view. Watch her route, then show it.

interaction.cue: Watch the signed reference route, then echo it.

record_publish.narration: You let the keeper post your account and how to find it. Pip writes the open questions right beside the view, where nobody can miss them. The younger keeper pins the guide up for visitors.

record_staff_copy.narration: You leave a copy that marks where a keeper must help. The younger keeper keeps it by her seat. She will explain the fixed date label to the next visitor.

memory_observation.narration: Water moves inside the ice, past a forked ridge and two rocks. Watch the river's path. Your boots stay on the floor while the old water rushes by.

interaction.cue: Watch the river pass the landmarks, then echo its course.

onSuccess.narration: Pip writes it down beside your crossing sketch. "Now let's check it from the other side."

onFailure.narration: You mark the part you missed instead of guessing. The second viewpoint can check it.

onAssisted.narration: Pip writes it down beside your crossing sketch. "Now let's check it from the other side."

close_view.narration: Your steady cradle makes the close view usable. Wait for the reflection to slide clear of the ridge.

interaction.cue: Record the ridge during the clear interval.

close_view_attuned.narration: Your steady cradle makes the close view usable. Wait for the reflection to slide clear of the ridge. Your starweaver uses a skill called Attune to feel the clear moment coming.

interaction.cue: Record the ridge during the clear interval.

dry_slips.narration: Your dry table kept the slips safe. You hand the clean stack to the younger keeper. Pip looks very proud of the dry paper, as if he invented it.

teach_live.narration: The newcomer stands beside you while the elder points out the landmarks. You show where you looked and where you stopped. With your help, the newcomer finds the safe view.

teach_posted.narration: The newcomer follows the posted guide alone. Watch the route markers, then show where to go.

interaction.cue: Watch the guide route, then echo it.

onSuccess.narration: The newcomer finds the view with the posted guide.

onFailure.narration: The newcomer misses a marker. The younger keeper steps in to help. A posted guide does not work for everyone.

onAssisted.narration: The newcomer misses a marker. The younger keeper steps in to help. A posted guide does not work for everyone.

teach_staff.narration: You hand your copy to the younger keeper, with the tricky parts marked. She walks the newcomer to the safe view. Nobody pretends they did it alone.

claim_limit_response_date.narration: The date stays open beside the checked observation. Now the question waits for the next reader.

claim_limit_response_cause.narration: The cause stays unanswered; nobody invents one. Now the question waits for the next reader.

claim_limit_response_compare.narration: The next comparison goes beside the clue, not in place of it. Now the question waits for the next reader.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Manticore scout. Eager but learns to separate observation from guess; never knows an unseen event.
npcVoices.Yeti keepers: Slow, enormous and gentle. Deliberate before answering. Offer a safe method and leave unknown history unknown.
